section_summary.extract_value: This Discussion section presents findings from a single study examining associations between exposure to nature and connectedness to nature with body appreciation in U.S. adult women and men. The study used the BAS-2 to assess body appreciation and employed online recruitment methods. Key findings include positive associations between both nature exposure and connectedness to nature with body appreciation, with self-esteem serving as a mediator for both women and men, and additional mediation pathways through motivational salience of appearance and internalisation of muscular ideals in men only.

This Discussion section presents findings from a study examining associations between nature exposure, connectedness to nature, and body appreciation in U.S. adult women and men. The study replicated previous work showing that connectedness to nature is positively associated with body appreciation and extended findings to show similar relationships between exposure to nature and body appreciation. Mediation pathways differed slightly between genders, with self-esteem mediating relationships in both groups, while motivational salience of appearance and internalisation of muscular ideals mediated relationships in men only.
